newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian chief prosecutor accused of drug ties.
newsitem.headline: Colombian chief prosecutor accused of drug ties.

text.p: The prosecutor who has campaigned to expose drug corruption at the highest levels of the Colombian government was accused of taking narcotics money for his personal benefit on Friday.
The accusation was made by Attorney General Orlando Vasquez Velasquez, who was suspended from office earlier this year because of his own alleged ties to drug lords.
Vasquez still faces possible criminal charges because of allegations that he received thousands of dollars in payments from top Colombian drug lords.
In remarks to reporters he said chief prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso, an anti-drug crusader long known as his personal nemesis, received drug money to back a failed bid for the Senate in 1994.
Valdivieso, a favourite of Washington whom polls regularly show to be one of Colombia's most respected public figures, had no immediate comment on Vasquez's allegation.

Valdivieso, whose office is run independently of the executive branch, filed criminal charges last February against President Ernesto Samper because of allegations that his 1994 election campaign was partly financed by drug kingpins.
The charges were dropped by Congress in June, however, on grounds that there was not enough evidence to support them.
